Indirect pneumatic brake (IP): The brake request is given by the DBV, the brake request is transferred by the DBV to a pressure level.

EVAPP.text: The EVAPP is energised directly by the emergency operation train line and the venting of the brake pipe is stopped.
The emergency brake application valve EVAPP is venting the brake pipe by the pre-controlled pneumatic application valve to allow a fast venting time via a large venting port.

In addition in case of failure to the emergency brake loop the "emergency mode" trainline is used to keep EVAPP valves (that are used to vent the brake pipe) energized allowing the train to move and escape from dangerous situations. 'Forward' and 'reverse' trainlines functionality shall not be affected.

3.5.1.1 Emergency Brake Application and Control Emergency brake application venting the brake pipe: The emergency brake loop is connected the emergency brake application valve EVAPP group 03.01/01 located in each DM car.

In case the emergency brake loop is de-energised the application magnet valve EVAPP will vent the pre-control pressure of the pneumatic application valve which opens the venting port for the brake pipe.

The emergency brake application valve group 03.01/01 has following components: − EVAPP magnet valve for venting pre-control pressure − Pneumatic application valve for venting the brake pipe − PAPP pressure switch 250 kPa for supervision of pneumatic valve application − RIVAPP emergency brake application valve isolation cock
The EVAPP supply from the emergency brake loop can be disconnected by brake pipe continuity test relay contact GC-K005.
In this case one REO relay contact disconnects the emergency brake loop to the emergency brake application valve EVAPP.

FAULTY.text: The indirect brake mode is used for the safe emergency brake and back-up indirect service brake in case of faulty direct brake.
If more than two cars have a faulty direct brake the driver is informed to switch to indirect service brake mode defined in chapter 3.2.
In case of faulty indirect brake the isolation cock RIEP-DIST 04.52 has to be isolated, in this case the complete car has no brake performance available and the auxiliary brake reservoir is vented.
If only the direct brake is faulty, the isolation cock RIEP 04.53 has to be isolated.
Based on this event and amount of faulty cars TCMS alarm is set to the driver to switch to indirect service brake mode (back-up mode).
Driver shall activate indirect service brake mode as specified in chapter 3.2 and isolate faulty DEP brake by isolation cock RIEP if necessary.

Therefore the isolation valve pre-control pressure electric magnet valve EVISO is directly hardwired connected to the cab active relay condition.
To isolate the brake pipe the EVISO shall be energized (high active command).

The train control logic will energise the EVISO valve to isolate the brake pipe and disable the brake pipe control and refill in following conditions:  Cab not active  Train in towed mode  Semi-automatic brake test by TCMS (BP continuity and tightness test)  Manual brake test switch in position BP isolation (BP continuity and tightness test) The EVISO valve can not be controlled directly by DBV-GW.

PB_SW.text: In case the parking brake is manually released the PB_SW is still indicating parking brake applied, refer to table 3.6.1.1 - T1.
The double contact switch-over micro switches PB_SW are read by TCMS and used for external parking brake status indication.
The status of the parking brake applied or released is set per bogie based on the parking brake calliper switches PB_SW status and BCU signal applied/released.
The electrical indicators are set by a combination of the caliper switches PB_SW, the manual release switch PBR_SW and the isolation cock status RIFS1/2.

MAU.text: The suppression system is designed at train level: the water/gas cylinders (MAU units) will be installed only in first and last coaches and there will be a pipe network with a main branch, going along the whole train and connecting the 2 MAU units, and suitable derivations to the sprinklers.
The suppression system is commanded by the detection system that activates both MAU units in case of fire.

3.3.5.1 Function Design 3.3.5.2 Normal condition As soon as the push button is pressed on either one of the control units, all the electrovalves on the MAU units will close and the water mist discharge is stopped.
Main components of the system are: MAU units (containing water cylinders and pressurized gas cylinders) and the stainless steel piping network with suitable nozzles for the water mist discharge.
Two MAU units are foreseen, one positioned in DM1 and one in DM8.

The piping network is constituted by a main branch connecting the 2 MAU units along the whole train and a secondary pipe in each coach where special nozzles, of sprinkler type including a thermal sensitive bulb, are connected.

In the Picture 7 below the position of the sprinklers and the MAU unit is shown in the first 2 coaches; in the other coaches the devices will be positioned symmetrically except for DM3 which will present a special configuration of sprinklers due to the particular layout of the coach.

EODJ.text: Normally, announcement balises are installed with successive execution balises in such a way that after a route distance of L1 = 1000m after the train crosses the announcement balise it crosses the corresponding execution balise and in doing so sends the high-active command S0 (EODJ = Exécution ouverture DJ) to the KVB.

With receipt of the signal S0 (EODJ), the TCMS system activates the pictogram VY_SECT on the driver desk for an additional route distance of d3 = L2 + d4 (d3 = 350m + 180m = 530m) regardless of which portion of route distance d1 has been covered after the announcement balise d4=180m =>ETR1000 IF Single unit length.
